name: manual_c67ec2
claim: Before applying a proposed security fix that reuses an existing auth/origin-check primitive, read that primitive's actual implementation and any documented design rationale — a function whose name suggests it blocks cross-origin requests may deliberately allow the specific origin you're trying to block, by design, for legitimate cross-service reasons

decisions.notes: Proposed adding verify_lifecycle_origin() to the G7 notification stream route to block a co-resident localhost:3000 app from reading the stream via a bootstrapped session cookie. Reading the actual function found it deliberately treats ALL loopback ports as mutually trusted (documented: portal :8002 must accept POSTs from pages served on PT :8000 or orama :8001) — the fix would have been a no-op while the accompanying test asserted a 403 the real code could never produce. Caught before committing by verifying the primitive's behavior instead of trusting its name/purpose inference.
